quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 5-4).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against dovish dissent

quote: Overall, the risks from inflation persistence appear to have continued to reduce. I therefore see scope for some further easing of policy.
rationale: Sees scope for further easing while voting to hold, a mild dovish lean against a market already pricing cuts.

quote: This does not mean that I expect to cut Bank Rate at any particular meeting. I will go into the coming meetings asking whether a cut is justified.
rationale: Meeting-by-meeting data dependence with no commitment either way.

quote: Monetary policy must, however, respond to the risk of a more persistent effect on UK CPI inflation.
rationale: Commits to respond to persistence risk: leans hawkish.

quote: Holding Bank Rate at this meeting is appropriate. I will be monitoring developments extremely closely and stand ready to act as necessary to ensure that inflation remains on track to meet the 2% target in the medium term.
rationale: Hold now but ready to act: leans hawkish (the +1 anchor).

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: For now, the softer real economy makes it appropriate to maintain Bank Rate.
rationale: Holds on activity grounds: leans dovish.

quote: I place some weight on Scenario C, which would require a stronger monetary policy response.
rationale: Acknowledges a tail that would need tighter policy.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 7-2).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Given the context at present of softness in the real economy and uncertainty around the scale and duration of the shock to energy prices, tolerating temporarily above-target inflation as part of a return to target is an appropriate way to approach the trade-off, providing inflation expectations remain contained.
rationale: Tolerates above-target inflation given soft activity: dovish tilt.

quote: I would respond promptly to any signals that an extended period of elevated energy prices could be leading to stronger possible second-round effects.
rationale: Readiness to respond: leans hawkish.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: There is little evidence yet of second-round effects (Boxes A and B), although it is too early to take much comfort from that.
rationale: Refuses comfort from benign data (rule 1): leans hawkish.

quote: Holding Bank Rate is appropriate as global conditions look to be more uncertain and inflationary, while domestic conditions are on balance more benign as regards the prospects for inflation.
rationale: Balanced hold.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: But if the conflict in the Middle East persists for an extended period, as appears to be the case, and the risk of second-round effects emerging increases, it is likely that policy may have to tighten.
rationale: Conditional case for tightening (rule 5 anchor).

quote: Financial conditions will continue to work to push down on inflation, and holding Bank Rate is appropriate at this meeting.
rationale: Conditions doing the work: leans dovish.

quote: The textbook response is to look through a one-off increase in the price level. Interest rates cannot produce more oil or gas, and monetary policy affects the economy with long lags. But looking through a shock is possible only if inflation expectations remain well anchored.
rationale: Looking through the shock only works while expectations stay anchored.

quote: If households and businesses begin to incorporate higher inflation into wage demands and pricing decisions, a temporary shock can become persistent. These second-round effects are slower to emerge.
rationale: Watch for second-round effects turning the shock persistent.

quote: Interest rates may need to rise even as economic activity weakens.
rationale: Rates may have to rise despite weaker activity.

quote: I remain sceptical of unconditional promises about future interest rates. The world is too uncertain. But central banks should explain clearly how policy would respond under different economic conditions.
rationale: Against forward guidance; no direction.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 4% (hike 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hike of 25bp to 4% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Absent this, risks to energy prices, and so to inflation, are to the upside.
rationale: Upside risks to inflation unless the conflict eases.

quote: Without news which softens the risks to inflationary pressures, I can see the argument for a further increase in rates and thereafter taking a more conditional approach, dependent on the evidence on energy prices and inflation dynamics.
rationale: Sees a case for one more hike then a conditional approach, short of the roughly 100bp the market prices.

quote: Recognising that some of the upward slope in the curve is explained by risk premia and not expected rates, the current level of restrictiveness is broadly appropriate.
rationale: Current restrictiveness broadly appropriate and the curve partly risk premia: less tightening than priced.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 5-4).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against dovish dissent

quote: Taken together, I prefer to hold Bank Rate at its current level. I am more concerned about the costs of cutting rates too quickly than too slowly, including the risks to credibility from any potential policy reversal that is not in response to a new shock.
rationale: Prefers a hold and fears cutting too quickly, against a market pricing cuts.

quote: While the near-term fall in CPI inflation should reduce second-round effects, it is not assured that wage growth will return to target-consistent rates (Box A).
rationale: Doubts wage growth will normalise: mild upside-risk language.

quote: I am prepared to act as needed to address any persistent inflationary effects that may emerge.
rationale: Readiness to act against persistent effects: leans hawkish.

quote: Policy coming into this shock may have been broadly neutral or mildly restrictive and there has since been some tightening of financial conditions.
rationale: Describes policy as only neutral to mildly restrictive, implying limited cushion.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: A tightening in monetary and financial conditions relative to before the war is warranted. Holding rates provides an appropriate degree of restrictiveness while we learn more about the scale of the shock and its propagation.
rationale: Endorses the market tightening and a hold: in line with expectations.

quote: While I do not view Scenario C as a central case, it is plausible, and would require policy to respond more forcefully to inflationary pressures.
rationale: Conditional tightening in a non-central scenario.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 7-2).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Holding Bank Rate remains appropriate as we learn more about the scale and duration of the shock and its propagation. Were signals to indicate inflation would persist above target, this would require policy to respond more forcefully to inflationary pressures.
rationale: Hold with a conditional forceful response: leans hawkish.

quote: There are risks for inflation in both directions.
rationale: Two-sided risks.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Policy would need to be adjusted were there to be evidence of risks of significant second-round effects, including from persistently higher energy prices.
rationale: Conditional case for tightening.

quote: The stance of monetary policy is restrictive, more so once broader financial conditions and the further underlying disinflation are factored in.
rationale: Restrictive stance language: leans dovish.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: The outlook for energy prices is uncertain and could change in the coming weeks, but the case for raising Bank Rate is building the longer the conflict continues without lasting resolution.
rationale: Case for a hike building: conditional tightening.

quote: The balance of risks to inflation has shifted more to the upside since our last policy decision.
rationale: Upside risks stressed.

quote: On that basis, policy is increasingly likely to need to tighten if elevated energy prices persist, absent clear evidence of disinflation or weaker activity.
rationale: Conditional case for tightening if energy prices persist.

quote: Finally, monetary policy should lean strongly against second-round effects, which risk de-anchoring inflation and preventing it from returning sustainably to target.
rationale: Lean strongly against second-round effects: hawkish tilt.

quote: But this is by no means suggesting that monetary policy should respond mechanically to movements in energy prices.
rationale: Balancing caveat against reacting to energy prices.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 4% (hike 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hike of 25bp to 4% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Cost pressures have remained elevated for sufficiently long that there is now a greater risk of second-round effects becoming embedded in price and wage-setting (Box A).
rationale: Greater risk of second-round effects becoming embedded.

quote: But overall I view the balance of risks to the inflation path as upside to our forecast given the ongoing energy price uncertainty and limited evidence of slack.
rationale: Inflation risks to the upside.

quote: In the absence of evidence of weaker inflation pressures, there is likely to be a case for a further increase in rates in the near term.
rationale: Likely another hike soon, then conditional: about in line with pricing.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.5%; decision 3.75% (hold 5-4).
rationale: dissent for a cut of 25bp to 3.5% against a majority hold at 3.75%

quote: I can see a case for taking out some insurance against these downside risks to inflation and think policy should be eased a little faster than implied by the current market path.
rationale: Wants easing faster than the market path, the -3 definition.

quote: But I place greater weight on downside risks, particularly in the near term, including those from an elevated household saving rate and a weakening labour market.
rationale: Downside risks weighted more heavily: clear dovish tilt.

quote: Absent this shock, the underlying disinflation process had continued broadly as I expected and, consistent with my vote in February, I would have expected to vote for a cut again in March.
rationale: Rule 13 anchor: a preference for easing that the shock only delays.

quote: How that adjustment occurs is hugely uncertain, with risks to both sides, and I vote to hold at this meeting.
rationale: Two-sided risks and a hold: balanced.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: This provides sufficient restrictiveness to guard against the current risk of second-round effects and gives us some time to learn more about the conflict and how it propagates.
rationale: Sufficient restrictiveness implies no need to tighten.

quote: I do not judge Scenario C as likely, but if it were to materialise, I would stand ready to react, forcefully if necessary, to return inflation to target sustainably.
rationale: Rubric anchor: stand ready to react, forcefully if necessary.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 7-2).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Monetary policy should look through the direct effects of the energy shock, partially through the indirect effects and act forcefully and early against any material second-round effects. The economic environment means the chance of material second-round effects is small and, although it is early days, there has been nothing in the news since April to change that assessment.
rationale: Look-through language and small second-round risk: dovish tilt.

quote: In my view, the current stance of financial conditions balances these risks, but I remain committed to acting early and decisively should material second‑round effects become likely.
rationale: Balanced now, with a commitment to act early.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Financial conditions facing households and businesses have tightened materially since the onset of the conflict, and consistent with the baseline, provide sufficient restrictiveness for now.
rationale: Sufficient restrictiveness implies no tightening needed.

quote: While my confidence around the domestic inflationary environment has increased, risks to global prices have shifted to the upside.
rationale: Global upside risks noted.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Material uncertainty is likely to continue, but if risks to the outlook for second-round effects crystallise, it becomes increasingly appropriate for Bank Rate to respond.
rationale: Conditional case for a hike (rubric +2 anchor).

quote: These make material second-round effects more likely, particularly if inflation approaches levels associated with non-linear effects.
rationale: Second-round risks rising: hawkish tilt.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 4% (hike 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hike of 25bp to 4% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: But with inflation expected to be above the threshold for non-linear effects, and little sign of a rapid or durable resolution to the conflict, the degree of inflationary pressure in the pipeline is now sufficient to warrant an increase in Bank Rate.
rationale: Pipeline inflation pressure now warrants a hike.

quote: The longer energy prices remain high the more likely persistent inflationary effects take hold, which would require further tightening in Bank Rate. But this will also depend on how energy prices propagate, especially given the risk that demand weakens.
rationale: Further tightening if energy stays high, but demand may weaken.

quote: For now, I judge the current restrictiveness of financial conditions as sufficient to balance these.
rationale: Current restrictiveness sufficient: no further hikes signalled against market pricing.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.5%; decision 3.75% (hold 5-4).
rationale: dissent for a cut of 25bp to 3.5% against a majority hold at 3.75%

quote: However, with my starting point for an estimate of the neutral rate of around 3%, I judge that policy should be less restrictive in order to meet the 2% target sustainably in the medium term.
rationale: Policy should be less restrictive with neutral at 3%: argues for easing.

quote: I see risks to the latest central projection for inflation as now tilted to the downside, reflecting the latest evidence and, in particular, the analysis presented in the February Report.
rationale: Inflation risks tilted down: clear dovish tilt.

quote: Data releases since the February Report have broadly been in line with my expectations, and suggested continuing disinflation, so I would have otherwise voted for a 25 basis point cut in Bank Rate at this meeting. The conflict has now led me to vote for a hold in Bank Rate.
rationale: Rule 13 anchor: would have cut but for the shock.

quote: I stand ready to act as necessary to ensure that CPI inflation remains on track to meet the 2% target in the medium term.
rationale: Generic readiness to act: leans hawkish.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Under Scenario B, I would consider raising Bank Rate and accepting a larger output gap as a result. If, however, some of the downside risks in Scenario A materialise, I would favour a less restrictive path.
rationale: Two-way conditional, tilted hawkish because Scenario B carries equal weight in his central view.

quote: Holding Bank Rate continues for me to be the most appropriate response to the ongoing uncertainty.
rationale: Hold under uncertainty.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 7-2).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Holding Bank Rate at this meeting keeps options open as we continue to learn more about the path of the conflict. My reaction function will remain state-contingent on both the development of the conflict, and what that means for the outlook for the economy.
rationale: State-contingent hold.

quote: Early, necessarily tentative, indications suggest that second-round effects might be limited, absent further escalation of the energy cost shock.
rationale: Second-round effects likely limited: leans dovish.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: If they were to crystallise, a hike in Bank Rate may be warranted. If the risks were to subside and the underlying disinflation process continued, I would consider resuming the cutting cycle.
rationale: Two-way conditional (rule 5).

quote: The policy stance is currently delivering the restrictiveness necessary to weigh against the upside risks posed by the global environment.
rationale: Restrictiveness is enough for now: leans dovish.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Overall, the risks to the inflation outlook have tilted more to the upside.
rationale: Rubric +2 anchor.

quote: Whilst the policy stance continues to provide restrictiveness, were upside pressures on the inflation outlook to continue to build, there could be a case for increasing Bank Rate.
rationale: Hedged conditional case for a hike.

quote: Indeed, with evidence that the disinflation process was on track at the time (and subsequently confirmed from my perspective with the data outturns we have seen this year) I would have expected at least two cuts by now, such that Bank Rate would be at least 0.5% below where it is today, and slightly below the UK OIS curve at the time (shown in Chart 8).
rationale: Absent the conflict he would have expected two cuts by now: holding only because of the shock.

quote: I think the tightening we have seen in financial conditions since the outbreak of the conflict, shown by the increase in the OIS curve since February, has helped to limit the potential for some of the direct effects from the energy shock to propagate through to second round effects.
rationale: Market tightening has helped limit second-round effects.

quote: But, as I set out in my individual paragraph in the September meeting minutes, I think the risks to the inflation outlook, whether external or domestically generated, have tilted more to the upside.
rationale: Risks tilted to the upside.

quote: Whilst the policy stance continues to provide restrictiveness, were upside pressures on the inflation outlook to continue to build, there could be a case for increasing Bank Rate.
rationale: Could be a case for a hike if pressure builds.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 4% (hike 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hike of 25bp to 4% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: I have also become somewhat less confident about the domestic disinflation process, the degree of slack, and how restrictive the policy stance has been to date.
rationale: Less confident on disinflation, slack and how restrictive policy is.

quote: Risks around the inflation outlook have shifted further to the upside.
rationale: Upside inflation risks.

quote: Nevertheless, households and firms’ resilience could weaken, with adjustment occurring through employment losses or business failures rather than prices.
rationale: Adjustment could come through job losses instead.

quote: A 25-basis point increase in Bank Rate is necessary now to ensure the appropriate degree of restrictiveness. I will continue to assess the evidence at each meeting, in particular how likely high energy prices are to feed through to other prices and the economy more broadly, by monitoring the evolution of pay, pricing behaviour, and slack.
rationale: Hike now, no commitment to more.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 5-4).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against dovish dissent

quote: I do not see a need to reduce Bank Rate further at this meeting.
rationale: Rejects a cut the market and four colleagues wanted.

quote: In that light, I continue to favour a cautious withdrawal of policy restriction, guided by longer‑term trends rather than short
rationale: Rule 13 anchor: slower cuts than the market wants scores hawkish.

quote: But monetary policy must contain potential second-round effects that would otherwise exert a more lasting impact on CPI inflation.
rationale: Policy must lean against second-round effects: hawkish tilt.

quote: I remain alert to those risks and stand ready to act if they intensify.
rationale: Readiness to act: leans hawkish.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 3.75% (hold 8-1).
rationale: dissent for a hike of 25bp to 4% against a majority hold at 3.75%

quote: As someone already concerned about a stalling of the underlying disinflation process even before the latest energy price shock, a prompt but modest hike in Bank Rate will help mitigate upside risks to price stability stemming from a re-emergence of intrinsic inflation persistence.
rationale: Argues for a hike now, explaining his dissent.

quote: But I see the risk of second-round effects in each of these scenarios as skewed to the upside.
rationale: Upside risks stressed.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 3.75% (hold 7-2).
rationale: dissent for a hike of 25bp to 4% against a majority hold at 3.75%

quote: Recognising the significant uncertainty that surrounds the UK inflation outlook, raising Bank Rate to 4% continues to be the most robust monetary policy response to the intensification of these risks.
rationale: Argues for raising Bank Rate to 4% now.

quote: While overall UK financial conditions have tightened since the conflict began, I continue to favour prompt but modest action on Bank Rate now.
rationale: Favours action on Bank Rate now.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: dissent for a hike of 25bp to 4% against a majority hold at 3.75%

quote: As a result, it is appropriate to raise Bank Rate now, thereby cutting through noise in commodity and asset price developments to offer a clear and unambiguous signal of our willingness and ability to address upside risks to inflation stemming from events in the Gulf.
rationale: Argues for a hike now.

quote: While energy prices remain volatile, risks to achieving the inflation target lie firmly to the upside.
rationale: Upside risks stressed.

quote: Given all this, I am uncomfortable with a ‘wait-and-see’ framing of the MPC’s current decisions over Bank Rate.
rationale: Rejects wait-and-see: argues tightening should come sooner than a hold implies.

quote: Turning to second-round effects, we should also be wary of believing uncertainties surrounding their strength will be resolved quickly.
rationale: Warns second-round uncertainty will not clear soon: leans hawkish.

quote: As reflected in my vote in recent policy rounds, I see benefit in acting clearly, promptly and decisively with Bank Rate.
rationale: Backs acting promptly and decisively (rule 3 jargon), tying it to his hike votes.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: dissent for a hike of 25bp to 4% against a majority hold at 3.75%

quote: A 25-basis point increase in Bank Rate now sends a clear signal of the MPC’s commitment to achieving its price stability mandate amidst the fog of geopolitical conflict and data noise.
rationale: Argues for a hike now.

quote: Acting decisively now cuts through in a way that bolsters the clarity and effectiveness of policy choices, thereby heading off inflationary pressures rather having to reverse them once they become ingrained.
rationale: Act decisively now (rule 3 jargon).

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 4% (hike 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hike of 25bp to 4% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Raising Bank Rate by 25 basis points at this meeting represents a significant step towards attaining the monetary policy stance needed to address current threats to price stability, including those stemming from uncertainty surrounding events in the Middle East and their influence over energy prices in the medium term.
rationale: The hike is a step toward the needed stance.

quote: Nonetheless, of itself, a single 25-basis point hike is unlikely to be sufficient. Achieving the level of Bank Rate necessary to confront challenges and risks to lasting achievement of the 2% inflation target is likely to require more policy tightening, including in the near term.
rationale: More tightening needed, including in the near term.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 5-4).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against dovish dissent

quote: New analysis and current developments have moved the appropriate time for a cut in Bank Rate closer.
rationale: A cut is coming closer, but not yet: leans dovish.

quote: A cut now would overweight the importance of the near-term mechanical disinflation and risk higher term premia.
rationale: Argues against cutting now, a mild hawkish lean given the market pricing cuts.

quote: Since the conflict may yield a sustained inflation shock, I see the balance between inflation and activity to have shifted away from considering a cut towards considering a longer hold, or even a hike at some point to lean against inflation persistence.
rationale: Moved from considering a cut to a longer hold or a hike: conditional case for tightening.

quote: Sustained pressure on energy prices could re-embed the inflation persistence of the last few years, through households’ salience to energy prices, firms’ state-dependent pricing, staggered wage contracts, and attentiveness thresholds.
rationale: Persistence risk is the main concern.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Should I see continued rising inflation outturns and expectations, I would expect to increase Bank Rate so as to lean against inflation rising into 2027.
rationale: Conditional hike: one level below an outright call.

quote: On balance, I expect greater additional second-round effects than in the scenarios.
rationale: Expects more second-round effects than staff: hawkish tilt.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 7-2).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: With sporadic continuance, uncertainty weighs on activity, but energy prices increase, which could trigger threshold effects: a worsening trade-off, but needing an activist hike.
rationale: Scenario-conditional case for an activist hike.

quote: Research shows that a forceful Bank Rate decision can have a quick effect on inflation and inflation expectations. So I have time to continue to evaluate measures of inflation expectations and financial restrictiveness to determine whether firms’ pricing and 2027 wage negotiations are on a target-consistent path for the medium term.
rationale: Holds for now while ready to act forcefully: balanced.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: dissent for a hike of 25bp to 4% against a majority hold at 3.75%

quote: A variety of research methods concludes that Bank Rate should be higher than 3.75% to return inflation to the 2% target sustainably.
rationale: Says Bank Rate should be higher now.

quote: Notwithstanding moderately restrictive nominal financial conditions, reinforcing policy credibility when faced with inflationary shocks implies that a 25 basis point increase in Bank Rate is appropriate at this time.
rationale: Argues for a 25bp hike now.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: dissent for a hike of 25bp to 4% against a majority hold at 3.75%

quote: Raising Bank Rate is a better risk-management strategy when faced with uncertainty about inflation dynamics and second-round effects.
rationale: Argues for a hike now.

quote: up until last week’s escalation in the Middle East, market participants had expected a prolonged Bank Rate hold, which was hard to square with achieving the 2% target.
rationale: Market path of a prolonged hold was too loose.

quote: In my view, our current monetary policy stance is not sufficiently tight, which is why I voted in the last two meetings for a 25 basis point increase in Bank Rate.
rationale: Rubric +4 anchor: stance not tight enough.

quote: At some point, we need to follow-through with Bank Rate rises – to maintain credibility, and to avoid policy expectations repricing downwards and inflation expectations repricing further upwards.
rationale: Further hikes needed to keep credibility.

quote: Given rising upside risks to inflation, a risk management strategy to monetary policy is appropriate.
rationale: Risk management strategy points to tightening.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4.25%; decision 4% (hike 8-1).
rationale: dissent for a larger move than the majority

quote: This projection is conditioned on a significant decline in energy prices; similar futures curves earlier this year have not eventuated. My policy strategy importantly is informed by research, which points to non-linear inflation risks.
rationale: Inflation projection relies on energy prices falling, which has not happened before.

quote: With CPI inflation at 3.5% in September, the economy has crossed the estimated statistical threshold into a high inflation-tight labour market regime where the asymmetric behavioural responses of households and firms support more robust second-round effects.
rationale: Economy in a high inflation regime with stronger second-round effects.

quote: Therefore, from a risk management and credibility perspective, a 50-basis point hike in Bank Rate is ‘good policy’.
rationale: Explicit call for an immediate 50bp hike, larger than the committee and the market.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.5%; decision 3.75% (hold 5-4).
rationale: dissent for a cut of 25bp to 3.5% against a majority hold at 3.75%

quote: The market-implied path for Bank Rate looks too tight. The costs of making a policy mistake seem much higher on the downside, especially given weak labour demand.
rationale: Says the market path is too tight, so wants easing sooner than priced.

quote: The inflation persistence scenario is less compelling given the prevailing weakness in activity and higher-than-expected unemployment.
rationale: Dismisses inflation persistence on weak activity: clear dovish tilt.

quote: If we see something resembling the lower-inflation scenario, I would expect to reduce Bank Rate, possibly quickly, over the rest of the year.
rationale: Conditional on the benign scenario, expects quick cuts: one level below an outright call for easing.

quote: This could warrant a hold or increase in Bank Rate to stabilise price-setting dynamics albeit creating a difficult trade-off with activity following a prolonged period of weakness.
rationale: Conditional opening to a hike in the severe scenario, hedged by the trade-off.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: In the event of a swift resolution and materially lower energy prices, further reduction in Bank Rate would be warranted, and possibly quickly.
rationale: Conditional on resolution, quick cuts.

quote: If the situation were to worsen, this may warrant some tightening, but there is a limit to how much output loss should be acceptable.
rationale: Conditional tightening heavily capped by output concerns.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 7-2).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: If the situation were to worsen, this may warrant some further tightening. But I do not see a compelling case to increase Bank Rate pre-emptively without new evidence of more intense first-round shocks.
rationale: Rule 13 anchor: stands against a hike.

quote: Absent the shock, monetary policy would be too restrictive for the cyclical position.
rationale: Policy too tight absent the shock: dovish tilt.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: An increase in Bank Rate now would be disproportionate as, unlike 2022, the starting point for this shock is much softer and the policy stance is more restrictive.
rationale: Argues against a hike now.

quote: I continue to see value in waiting for a clearer read on the energy shock in the coming months before deciding whether a change in policy is required, given the broad range of possible outcomes.
rationale: Rubric -2 anchor phrase.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: I therefore continue to see value in waiting for a clearer read on the durable scale of the shock over the coming months, including evidence on first-round energy effects and the conditions for 2027 wage and price-setting.
rationale: Prefers waiting (rubric -2 anchor).

quote: With consumption subdued, vacancies below pre-pandemic levels and margins not expanding, the domestic economy appears unlikely to sustain second-round effects that would magnify the initial impulse.
rationale: Dismisses second-round risk: dovish tilt.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 4% (hike 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hike of 25bp to 4% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Broad-based price pressures remain subdued, however, and we cannot yet distinguish between delayed pass-through and weaker pass-through on the evidence available (Box A).
rationale: Broad price pressures subdued.

quote: Raising Bank Rate by 25 basis points provides additional insurance against upside risks from stronger pass-through and firmer growth in demand.
rationale: Backs the hike as insurance.

quote: To support maintaining Bank Rate at a higher level for an extended period, I would need to see clear evidence of a recovery in firms’ pricing power and households’ purchasing power alongside signs of mutually reinforcing wage and price pressures.
rationale: Sets a high bar for keeping rates higher for long, signalling a short-lived hike.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 5-4).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against dovish dissent

quote: I continue to think the monetary policy stance is not materially restrictive. Finally, I believe the cost of a policy error is greater if Bank Rate follows the market path and we end up with inflation persistence versus weaker demand.
rationale: Stance not restrictive and following the market path risks persistence: wants tighter than priced.

quote: I would prefer to wait to see that firms and households revise down their inflation expectations in response to lower realised inflation.
rationale: Prefers to delay cuts the market expects until expectations fall.

quote: The risk of inflation persistence has risen, perhaps significantly, in light of the negative supply shock from the war in the Middle East.
rationale: Persistence is the main concern: clear hawkish tilt.

quote: It is appropriate to hold Bank Rate to learn more about the size and duration of the shock, and the extent of potential second-round effects.
rationale: Data-dependent hold.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: We may end up with inflation somewhere between Scenarios B and C, necessitating a tighter stance.
rationale: Conditional case for a tighter stance.

quote: An increase in Bank Rate may be necessary in upcoming meetings.
rationale: Flags a likely hike soon.

quote:
But I think it’s most likely that we’ll end up with second-round effects somewhere 
between Scenarios B and C: let’s call it Scenario M for Megan.
rationale: Expects second-round effects above the central scenario: hawkish tilt.

quote:
In addition to having a worse inflation outcome, I think a prolonged hold strategy lacks 
credibility in Scenario M.
rationale: A prolonged hold lacks credibility: argues for tightening.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 3.75% (hold 7-2).
rationale: dissent for a hike of 25bp to 4% against a majority hold at 3.75%

quote: These risks are asymmetric, so we should insure against the possibility of larger second-round effects until we have evidence to determine they are not materialising. A proactive hike now in Bank Rate should help anchor inflation expectations.
rationale: Argues for a hike now.

quote: Given significant uncertainty about the extent of second-round effects, we should pursue a risk management strategy.
rationale: Risk management jargon points to tightening.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: dissent for a hike of 25bp to 4% against a majority hold at 3.75%

quote: As in June, there is significant uncertainty about which projection or scenario is most likely and I believe a risk management strategy is appropriate.
rationale: Risk management strategy points to tightening.

quote: Furthermore, a proactive hike in Bank Rate may reduce the probability that second-round effects set in.
rationale: Argues for a proactive hike.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: dissent for a hike of 25bp to 4% against a majority hold at 3.75%

quote: Waiting for definitive evidence of second-round effects before acting would leave policy behind the curve, and we cannot rely on premia to do our work for us.
rationale: Behind-the-curve argument (rubric +3 anchor).

quote: But resilience in labour demand and activity suggest slack may have already peaked.
rationale: Slack may have peaked: hawkish tilt.

quote: I believe the evidence laid out in this speech shows the risk of second-round effects is greater than we thought. Furthermore, staff simulations suggest setting policy as if you were in a stronger second-round effects scenario and then adjusting policy upon learning you are in a minimal second-round effects scenario leads to better outcomes than doing the opposite. I therefore continue to believe we should proactively lean against the risk of second-round effects.
rationale: Wants to lean proactively against second-round effects; with about 97bp of hikes priced, this is a hawkish tilt rather than a call beyond the market.

quote: It is not obvious to me from this data that our monetary policy stance is meaningfully restrictive.
rationale: Doubts policy is restrictive (milder than the +4 anchor), against a market already pricing hikes.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 4% (hike 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hike of 25bp to 4% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Evidence of second-round effects has remained scant as expected, but the risks have clearly shifted to the upside.
rationale: Risks shifted clearly to the upside.

quote: I believe the output gap is smaller than we think and has likely peaked.
rationale: Less slack than assumed.

quote: We continue to face Knightian uncertainty, but a rate hike now is appropriate based on the central outlook rather than just risk management considerations. Additional hikes will likely be required going forward, though further out this will depend on pay, pricing behaviour and slack.
rationale: Hike on the central outlook, and more hikes likely needed.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.5%; decision 3.75% (hold 5-4).
rationale: dissent for a cut of 25bp to 3.5% against a majority hold at 3.75%

quote: If we expect to be at or below the target with significant slack emerging in about six months, a neutral rate of 3% should be in our sights now.
rationale: Wants rates moving to neutral now, easing sooner than priced.

quote: Together with normalising wages (Boxes A and B), all this reduces or even eliminates the risk of the inflation persistence scenario.
rationale: Says persistence risk is reduced or gone: clear dovish tilt.

quote: Given massive uncertainty around future energy prices, I currently see a high bar to hiking. I prefer to hold while we better gauge the shock.
rationale: High bar to hiking and prefers to hold: dovish against a market moving toward hikes.

quote: This could imply faster and potentially deeper rate cuts, once inflation risks subside, to avoid being behind the curve.
rationale: Sees faster and deeper cuts once risks subside.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: This would entail a hold for some time, then a move to a neutral or accommodative stance.
rationale: Expects to move to neutral or below after a hold.

quote: Given neutral at 3%, it makes sense to hold, for risk-management reasons and because the tighter financial conditions since the conflict began are amply restrictive to provide insurance against inflation risks if we eventually face the not-implausible Scenario B or the more extreme Scenario C.
rationale: Amply restrictive conditions mean no hike needed.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 7-2).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Absent worse news, I cannot see a case for tightening now, and an active hold is reasonable. If the conflict resolution holds, and risks diminish, lower rates could be preferred.
rationale: No case to tighten and lower rates possible: argues policy is tight enough.

quote: Policy is restrictive, 75 basis points above my estimate of neutral and where we might have been quite soon.
rationale: Policy well above neutral: dovish.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: For me, the more likely outcomes sit between the baseline and milder scenario, albeit with a long right tail; keeping Bank rate on hold, at a higher level now than the pre-conflict implied path, gives insurance for now, before resuming cuts when and if geopolitical uncertainty clears.
rationale: Hold as insurance, then resume cuts.

quote: The economy is drifting further toward deficient demand, with material risk of larger output gaps, labour-market scarring, and a slowdown in growth over the next year or two.
rationale: Growth concerns dominate: dovish tilt.

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: My view is that additional tightening is not warranted at present.
rationale: Against tightening now.

quote: Equally, if geopolitical tensions abate and inflation pressures ease, an easing of policy should be in sight.
rationale: Conditional easing in sight.

quote: My view is that the current stance is also sufficiently restrictive, given the initial conditions of the economy in which the shock is hitting.
rationale: Stance sufficiently restrictive: no tightening needed.

quote: However, it does suggest, to me, that the burden of proof for additional tightening should rest on evidence that second-round effects are actually gaining traction, rather than on the existence of the energy shock alone.
rationale: Sets a high bar for tightening.

quote: But symmetrically, if the economy evolves broadly as expected, with demand weakening and underlying domestic inflationary pressures continuing to moderate, then at some point, once energy risks abate, policy will need to move in the other direction
rationale: Expects eventual easing once energy risks abate (conditional).

quote: Voted for Bank Rate at 4%; decision 4% (hike 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hike of 25bp to 4% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: It is essential to communicate, and for markets to understand, that, as of now, this is not the start of a hiking cycle: policy isn’t on a pre-set, unconditional path. The risk is curve dislocation and unwarranted tightening in financial conditions.
rationale: Not the start of a hiking cycle: argues against the path the market prices.

quote: Rather, from an already restrictive position, this is a risk-management ‘one-for-now’ insurance hike.
rationale: A one-for-now insurance hike from a restrictive stance.

quote: The next move could be up, down, or sideways.
rationale: Open to a cut next, against priced hikes.

quote: Voted for the policy rate at 0.75%; decision 0.75% (hold 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 0.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: 金融政策運営は、現在の実質金利がきわめて低い水準にあることを踏まえますと、以上のような経済・物価の見通しが実現していくとすれば、経済・物価情勢の改善に応じて引き続き政策金利を引き上げ、金融緩和度合いを調整していくことになると考えています。
quote_en: As for the conduct of monetary policy, given that real interest rates are currently at significantly low levels, if the outlook for economic activity and prices presented so far is realized, the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation in accordance with improvement in economic activity and prices.
rationale: Governor restating the committee's path of gradual hikes (rule 7).

quote: こうした金融環境を介して、政策変更の影響が実体経済や物価に広く波及するまでにはかなりの時間を要すると考えられますが、日本銀行としては過去の利上げを含めて企業や家計の行動や経済・物価に及ぼす様々な影響を丁寧に点検してまいりたいと考えています。
quote_en: It is likely to take considerable time for the effects of policy changes to spread widely through the real economy and prices via these financial conditions, but the Bank intends to examine carefully the various effects, including those of past rate hikes, on the behavior of firms and households and on economic activity and prices.
rationale: Will check the effects of past hikes carefully: leans cautious.

quote: Voted for the policy rate at 0.75%; decision 0.75% (hold 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 0.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: 金融政策運営は、現在の実質金利がきわめて低い水準にあることを踏まえますと、以上のような経済・物価の見通しが実現していくとすれば、経済・物価情勢の改善に応じて、引き続き政策金利を引き上げ、金融緩和の度合いを調整していくことになると考えています。
quote_en: As for the conduct of monetary policy, given that real interest rates are currently at significantly low levels, if the outlook for economic activity and prices presented so far is realized, the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation in accordance with improvement in economic activity and prices.
rationale: Governor restating the committee's path (rule 7).

quote: なお、原油価格上昇が基調的な物価上昇率の見通しに及ぼす影響についても留意が必要です。
quote_en: We also need to pay attention to the effect of higher crude oil prices on the outlook for underlying inflation.
rationale: Flags oil's effect on underlying inflation.

quote: そのうえで今後の決定会合等に向けてということでありますと、これは私いつも申し上げていることですけれども、今、原油価格が上がって、これがまず景気という意味では交易条件を悪化させるということを通じて景気に下押し圧力となる。
quote_en: Looking ahead to the coming Monetary Policy Meetings, as I always say, higher crude oil prices first put downward pressure on the economy by worsening the terms of trade.
rationale: Balanced: oil weighs on activity and adds to inflation.

quote: Voted for the policy rate at 0.75%; decision 0.75% (hold 6-3).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 0.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: これらのリスクがともに高まることも考えられますが、基調的な物価上昇率が2%に近づいている中、企業の賃金・価格設定行動が積極化していることなどを踏まえますと、特に物価上昇率が大きく上振れていくリスクが顕在化し、それがその後の経済に悪影響を及ぼすことがないよう十分に留意する必要があります。
quote_en: Both of these risks could rise together, but with underlying inflation approaching 2% and firms' wage- and price-setting behavior becoming more active, we need to pay close attention in particular to the risk that inflation overshoots significantly and that this then harms the economy.
rationale: Stresses the risk of inflation overshooting.

quote: 物価面ですが、中東情勢に伴う景気減速は、需給ギャップの悪化などを通じて、基調的な物価上昇率を下押す方向に作用するものの、全体としてみれば上振れリスクの方が大きいと考えています。
quote_en: On prices, the economic slowdown caused by the situation in the Middle East will push down on underlying inflation through a worsening output gap, but overall we think the upside risks are larger.
rationale: Upside price risks larger overall.

quote: 日本銀行としては、基調的な物価上昇率が2%に近づいている中、現在の実質金利がきわめて低い水準にあることを踏まえますと、経済・物価・金融情勢に応じて、引き続き政策金利を引き上げ、金融緩和の度合いを調整していくことになると考えています。
quote_en: With underlying inflation approaching 2% and real interest rates currently at significantly low levels, the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation in accordance with economic activity, prices and financial conditions.
rationale: Governor restating the committee's path (rule 7).

quote: それから、インフレ期待のところについても、まだ確たることは申し上げられませんが、少し古くなりますが、短観の企業の物価に対する見方とか、あるいは足元のブレーク・イーブン・インフレ率の動きとか、ちょっと上振れているところがありますので、これは注視してみていきたいなと思っております。
quote_en: On inflation expectations, I cannot yet say anything definitive, but firms' views on prices in the Tankan, although a little dated, and recent moves in break-even inflation rates show some upward drift, so we want to watch this closely.
rationale: Inflation expectations edging up; watching closely.

quote: If, for example, the Bank judges that the likelihood of realizing the baseline scenario will rise, in that tension over the situation in the Middle East will gradually ease and that underlying CPI inflation will gradually rise toward 2 percent on the back of moderate economic growth, I think the Bank will c ontinue to raise the policy interest rate at an appropriate pace.
rationale: Governor restating the expected path of gradual hikes (rule 7).

quote: Meanwhile, even if the situation remains unclear, should it be judged that upside risks to prices outweigh downside risks to economic activity , it will be necessary to thoroughly discuss the pros and cons of raising the policy interest rate, from the perspective of preventing adverse effects on the economy and financial markets and achieving the price stability target of 2 percent in a sustainable and stable manner.
rationale: Opens the door to a hike even under uncertainty if price risks dominate.

quote: A basic principle, therefore, is that monetary policy should not seek to address such inflation.
rationale: Look through supply-shock inflation: leans dovish.

quote: Voted for the policy rate at 1%; decision 1% (hold 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 1% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: 日本銀行としては、基調的な物価上昇率が2%に近づいている中、現在の金融環境が緩和的であることを踏まえますと、経済・物価・金融情勢に応じて、引き続き政策金利を引き上げ、金融緩和の度合いを調整していくことになると考えています。
quote_en: With underlying inflation approaching 2% and financial conditions currently accommodative, the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation in accordance with economic activity, prices and financial conditions.
rationale: Governor restating the committee's path (rule 7).

quote: 特に、基調的な物価上昇率が2%の物価安定の目標を超えて上振れていくリスクが顕在化し、それがその後の経済に悪影響を及ぼすことがないよう、基調的な物価上昇率を2%程度の水準で安定させていくという観点が重要になると考えています。
quote_en: In particular, we think it will become important to stabilize underlying inflation at around 2%, so that the risk of it overshooting the 2% price stability target does not materialize and then harm the economy.
rationale: Priority on keeping underlying inflation from overshooting 2%.

quote: そのうえで、もう一度そのときお話ししたような基本的な考え方を繰り返させて頂きますと、そのとき申し上げた通りですが、金融緩和度合いの調整のタイミング、あるいはペースについては、そのとき申し上げた三つのポイント、中東情勢とそれからAI関連の動き、そして為替相場の変動の影響、これらを特に重視しつつ、経済・物価の中心的な見通しが実現する確度、あるいはその周りのリスクを点検しながら検討していくという基本的な考え方です。
quote_en: Let me repeat the basic thinking I set out then: on the timing and pace of adjusting the degree of monetary accommodation, we will consider them while examining the likelihood of the baseline outlook for economic activity and prices being realized and the surrounding risks, putting particular weight on the three points I mentioned, the situation in the Middle East, AI-related developments and the effects of exchange rate movements.
rationale: Governor restating the approach; no pushback on market pricing of a September hike.

quote: Voted for the policy rate at 1.25%; decision 1.25% (hike 7-2).
rationale: majority vote for a hike of 25bp to 1.25% at a split meeting, against dovish dissent

quote: 今後の金融政策運営については、基調的な物価上昇率が2%に近づいている中、現在の金融環境が緩和的であることを踏まえますと、経済・物価・金融情勢に応じて引き続き政策金利を引き上げ、金融緩和の度合いを調整していくことになると考えています。
quote_en: As for the future conduct of monetary policy, with underlying inflation approaching 2% and financial conditions currently accommodative, the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation in accordance with economic activity, prices and financial conditions.
rationale: Governor restating the committee's path (rule 7).

quote: 特に、基調的な物価上昇率が2%の物価安定の目標を超えて上振れていくリスクが顕在化し、それがその後の経済に悪影響を及ぼすことがないよう、基調的な物価上昇率を2%程度の水準で安定させていくという観点が重要になると考えています。
quote_en: In particular, we think it will become important to stabilize underlying inflation at around 2%, so that the risk of it overshooting the 2% price stability target does not materialize and then harm the economy.
rationale: Priority on keeping underlying inflation from overshooting 2%.

quote: こうしたことの私どもの政策への含意ですけれども、基本姿勢を申し上げることにとどまりますけれども、基調的な物価上昇率が2%に近づいている中で、一方で金融環境がいつも申し上げている通り緩和的な状態が続いているということですので、基本的には引き続き政策金利を、経済・物価・金融情勢に応じてですけれども、引き上げて、緩和度合いを調整していくというふうになると考えています。
quote_en: As for the implications for our policy, I can only state our basic stance: with underlying inflation approaching 2% while financial conditions, as I always say, remain accommodative, the Bank will basically continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of accommodation, in accordance with economic activity, prices and financial conditions.
rationale: Governor restating the committee's path (rule 7).

quote: 9月の決定会合後の会見で申し上げたことと重なりますけれども、その際に、基調物価が2%にかなり接近しているという中では、基調物価の上昇率を2%程度で安定させていくという観点がこれまでよりも重要になってくるというふうに考えております。
quote_en: This overlaps with what I said at the press conference after the September meeting: with underlying inflation very close to 2%, stabilizing it at around 2% is becoming more important than before.
rationale: Stabilising underlying inflation at 2% matters more than before.

quote: Voted for the policy rate at 1.25%; decision 1.25% (hold 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 1.25% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: 基調的な物価上昇率が2%の物価安定の目標と概ね整合的な水準となる中、企業の賃金・価格設定行動が積極化していることや、様々な物価上振れ要因を踏まえますと、中長期的な予想物価上昇率が上昇し、基調的な物価上昇率が2%の物価安定の目標を超えて上振れていくリスクがあります。
quote_en: With underlying CPI inflation broadly consistent with the 2 percent price stability target, and given that firms' wage- and price-setting behavior has become more active and the various factors pushing up prices, there is a risk that medium- to long-term inflation expectations rise and underlying CPI inflation overshoots the 2 percent target.
rationale: Risk that underlying inflation overshoots 2 percent as expectations rise.

quote: 私どもとしては、基調的な物価上昇率が2%の物価安定の目標と概ね整合的な水準となる中、現在の金融環境が緩和的であることを踏まえますと、経済・物価・金融情勢に応じて、引き続き政策金利を引き上げ、金融緩和の度合いを調整していくことになると考えています。
quote_en: With underlying CPI inflation broadly consistent with the 2 percent price stability target, and given that current financial conditions are accommodative, we expect to continue raising the policy interest rate and adjusting the degree of monetary accommodation in accordance with developments in economic activity, prices and financial conditions.
rationale: The Governor restates the path: keep raising rates as conditions allow.

quote: それから、どういうときに、well positionedというふうに言えるかという二番目のご質問ですが、抽象的には概ね政策金利が中立金利に達して上下両方向のショックに機動的に対応できるという状態ということだと思いますけれども、それがいつどういうふうに判断できるかという点に関しては、現実にはなかなかそう簡単に今そこに達したという判断が難しいということは、これまでお話してきた通りでございまして、これまで何回か利上げをしてきておりますが、その累積的な影響を確認、および何度も申し上げてるような、同時に金融環境をよくみるということを、その一部が累積的な影響を確認していく作業であるわけですけれども、みながら少しずつ確認していくしかないなというふうに思っています。
quote_en: On your second question, when we can say we are well positioned: in the abstract, it is a state in which the policy rate has broadly reached the neutral rate and we can respond nimbly to shocks in either direction. But as I have said before, in practice it is not easy to judge when we have reached that point. We have raised rates several times, and the only way forward is to confirm their cumulative effects, which is partly what watching financial conditions closely means, and to check this little by little as we go.
rationale: Hard to tell when neutral is reached; will check step by step.

quote: 私どもの考え方としては、機動的に利上げできるかどうかということよりも、これまでは基調物価が2[%]を下回ってる中で、基調物価が少し上昇するということは、ある種容認されることで、2[%]に上がっていくことがある種狙いですので、これからはもう2[%]に達してますので、ある程度目にみえて上がるということは望ましくないことであると。従ってそういうことを考えますと、上振れリスクには適宜対応しないといけないということが導かれるという考え方でございます。
quote_en: Our thinking is less about whether we can raise rates nimbly. Until now, with underlying inflation below 2 percent, some rise in underlying inflation was in a sense acceptable, since reaching 2 percent was the aim. Now that it has reached 2 percent, a visible further rise is undesirable. It follows that we need to respond to upside risks as appropriate.
rationale: With underlying inflation at 2 percent, further rises are unwelcome, so upside risks must be met.

quote: Voted for the policy rate at 0.75%; decision 0.75% (hold 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 0.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Voted for the policy rate at 0.75%; decision 0.75% (hold 8-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 0.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Voted for the policy rate at 0.75%; decision 0.75% (hold 6-3).

rationale: Commitment to price stability "strong, unanimous, and unambiguous".

quote: Today, as you know, our Committee decided to vote by a 9-to-3 vote to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3½ to 3¾ percent.
rationale: The Chair restates the hold.

quote: If inflation continues to be elevated through the forecast period, interest rates could well be part of that solution.
rationale: Conditional opening to higher rates if inflation stays high.

quote: Any central banker, especially a central banker where the labor markets are more or less at equilibrium—any central banker, when he or she sees underlying inflation moving higher—he or she is more inclined to tighten policy.
rationale: With jobs at equilibrium and underlying inflation rising, more inclined to tighten.

quote: None of these measures are perfect, but they all tell a similar story: Inflation is running above our 2 percent target. So the Fed's predominant focus right now should be on prices.
rationale: The Fed should focus predominantly on prices.

quote: A good majority of my colleagues and I thought the wiser course was to await new information in the intermeeting period—especially given possible developments in supply chains, investment flows, and geopolitics—before deciding whether a change in interest rate policy was advisable. And we expressed our joint readiness to act as circumstances might require.
rationale: Waited for information in July, with a stated readiness to act.

quote: The good news is that measures of inflation expectations in the medium term, by and large, look stable.
rationale: Medium-term expectations stable.

quote: Here is my standard: We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do.
rationale: Unless inflation is clearly falling fast enough, there is work to do.

quote: In the meeting just concluded, the FOMC decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by a ¼ percentage point to 3¾ to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve’s dual mandate.
rationale: The Chair restates the committee hike.

quote: Inflation is the problem.  Stable prices have been the problem for now more than five and a half years.  So what the Committee decided to do today was take an action to ensure a timelier return to our price-stability objective.
rationale: Inflation is the problem; the hike was to ensure a timelier return to target.

quote: Voted for the top of the fed funds target range at 4%; decision 4% (hold 10-2).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 4% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: The Committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal.
rationale: More information will decide the stance: no lean beyond the expected path.

quote: so what I can do is tell you, there's no soft inflation target. There's no implicit inflation target. There's a target of price stability and it's 2 percent as measured by PCE.
rationale: No tolerance for a softer inflation target.

quote: Is the economy running too hot? Is the economy running too strong?  That isn’t the judgement of most of my colleagues.
rationale: Most colleagues do not see the economy running too hot, against pricing of more hikes.

quote: In my view, those moves have brought the federal funds rate into a range consistent with the neutral rate — a rate that neither stimulates nor restricts economic activity.
rationale: Rate already near neutral, weakening the case for more cuts.

quote: While I do not want to prejudge the decision that will take place there, in my view, the current policy stance leaves us well positioned to determine the extent and timing of additional adjustments to our policy rate based on the incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks.
rationale: Data-dependent on the extent and timing of further moves.

quote: While some upside risks remain, moving forward I expect to see inflation return to a sustainable path back to our 2 percent target. It is a reasonable base case that the effects of tariffs on inflation will not be long-lasting—effectively, a one-time shift in the price level.
rationale: Expects tariff effects to be one-time and inflation to return to target.

quote: In this less dynamic and somewhat softer labor market, the downside risks to employment appear to have risen.
rationale: Downside risks to employment have risen.

quote: Voted for the top of the fed funds target range at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 10-2).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against dovish dissent

quote: Collectively, these adjustments put our policy rate broadly in the range of estimates of the neutral rate while maintaining a balanced approach to promoting our dual-mandate objectives.
rationale: Rate near neutral after the cuts, so less need to move again soon.

quote: Certainly, some upside risks remain, but I expect the disinflationary process to resume this year once increased tariffs pass through more fully to prices.
rationale: Expects disinflation to resume this year.

quote: All other things being equal, persistent increases in productivity growth are likely to result in an increase in the neutral rate, at least temporarily.
rationale: Higher productivity growth points to a higher neutral rate.

quote: Voted for the top of the fed funds target range at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 11-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against dovish dissent

quote: These changes put the rate broadly in the range of neutral while maintaining a balanced approach to promoting our dual-mandate objectives. The current policy stance should continue to support the labor market while allowing inflation to resume its decline toward our 2 percent target as the effects of tariff pass-through are completed.
rationale: Rate near neutral; stance supports jobs while inflation falls.

quote: In the U.S., the increase in energy prices to date should have relatively modest effects on inflation, though consumers are seeing higher gas prices at the pump now.
rationale: Energy price rise so far has modest effects on inflation.

quote: As a monetary policymaker I confront an outlook where there is downside risk to the labor market and upside risk to inflation. While that is a potentially challenging situation, I am confident that our current policy stance is well positioned to respond to a range of outcomes.
rationale: Two-sided risks; policy well positioned.

quote: I am highly attentive to the fact that inflation has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five years.
rationale: Attentive to five years of above-target inflation.

quote: Inflation has eased from its pandemic-era peak, but progress has stalled over the past year mainly due to tariffs. In addition, I expect elevated energy prices will be reflected in upcoming inflation readings.
rationale: Disinflation stalled, energy to push readings up.

quote: This adjustment put the rate broadly in the range of neutral, or a rate that neither stimulates nor constrains the economy. The current stance should continue to support the labor market while allowing inflation to resume its decline toward our 2 percent target as the effects of tariff pass-through are completed.
rationale: Rate near neutral; balanced stance.

quote: I expect inflation to decline later this year as the effects of tariffs and the energy shock wane, but I view risks around my inflation outlook as tilted to the upside.
rationale: Inflation to fall later this year, with upside risks: balanced.

quote: I see risks to the labor market as somewhat skewed to the downside.
rationale: Downside labour market risks.

quote: I believe this policy stance leaves us well positioned to respond to economic developments based on the incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. I have not prejudged the next meeting and look forward to engaging with my colleagues about the policy necessary to best achieve our dual-mandate goals.
rationale: Well positioned, not prejudging the next meeting.

quote: The quick succession of shocks raises the risk that inflation becomes entrenched and inflation expectations become unanchored.
rationale: Succession of shocks risks entrenching inflation.

quote: That said, in a scenario where actual inflation does not start to cool down soon, I believe that it could be appropriate to reconsider our current policy stance to ensure we fulfill our commitment to deliver price stability.
rationale: Could reconsider the stance if inflation does not cool soon.

quote: If AI indeed raises the neutral rate, then for any given level of the federal funds rate, policy effectively becomes more accommodative.
rationale: A higher neutral rate would make current policy more accommodative.

quote: This was an important step to ensure longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored and to validate the public's confidence that we will achieve our 2 percent inflation objective in a timely manner.
rationale: The hike protects expectations.

quote: But if actual inflation remains above our target, then households and businesses may eventually stop believing that we will return inflation to 2 percent.
rationale: Risk that expectations drift if inflation stays high.

quote: Since our September meeting, yields across the term structure have increased further, a sign that investors are reassessing the evolving macroeconomic landscape. rationale: Will take time to judge, not endorsing the market move toward more hikes.

quote: Voted for the top of the fed funds target range at 4%; decision 4% (hold 10-2).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 4% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: With inflation on a sustained trajectory toward 2 percent and signs of fragility in the labor market, my view is that we should continue to focus on risks to our employment mandate and preemptively stabilize and support labor market conditions.
rationale: Wants policy to preemptively support the labour market, that is, further cuts.

quote: Absent a clear and sustained improvement in labor market conditions, we should remain ready to adjust policy to bring it closer to neutral. We should also avoid signaling that we will pause without identifying that conditions have changed.
rationale: Ready to cut toward neutral and against signalling a pause.

quote: However, after removing estimated tariff effects, core PCE inflation would have hovered close to 2 percent in recent months, well below the 3 percent reading at the end of 2024.
rationale: Underlying inflation near target once tariffs are excluded.

quote: Voted for the top of the fed funds target range at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 10-2).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against dovish dissent

quote: I continue to see policy as moderately restrictive, and, looking ahead to 2026, my Summary of Economic Projections includes three cuts for this year.
rationale: Projects three cuts this year and sees policy as restrictive.

quote: But we have seen some signs of stabilization, and, after lowering the policy rate by a total of 75 basis points in the latter part of last year, in my view, we can afford to take time and "keep policy powder dry" for a little while in order to carefully assess how the lower degree of policy restraint is flowing through to broader financial conditions and strengthening the labor market.
rationale: Accepts a short pause while still wanting cuts.

quote: However, absent a clear and sustained improvement in labor market conditions, we should be ready to adjust policy to bring it closer to neutral. rationale: Ready to cut toward neutral and against signalling an extended hold.

quote: The underlying trend in core PCE inflation appears to be moving much closer to our 2 percent target than is currently showing in the data.
rationale: Underlying inflation closer to target than the data show.

quote: Voted for the top of the fed funds target range at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 11-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against dovish dissent

quote: As I think about the path forward for monetary policy, I would like to have more clarity on the economic impacts from the conflict in the Middle East and the durability of those effects. In this regard, I appreciated and supported keeping the language from the March post-meeting statement about additional policy rate adjustments.
rationale: Supported keeping the easing language about additional adjustments.

quote: Reacting to temporarily elevated energy price inflation would add unwarranted policy restraint, weighing unnecessarily on economic activity and labor market conditions.
rationale: Argues to look through the energy shock rather than tighten.

quote: But the longer the conflict persists, the more we should consider the effects on inflation in our outlook. In particular, the more persistent higher oil prices are—or if we start to see broader effects of higher energy prices on PCE inflation—the more likely I will consider shifting my approach to thinking about the balance of risks.
rationale: A long conflict would make her weigh inflation more.

rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

quote: Having lowered our policy rate by 75 basis points over the course of our previous three meetings, we see the current stance of monetary policy as appropriate to promote progress toward both our maximum-employment and 2 percent inflation goals.
rationale: The Chair describes the current stance as appropriate after the cuts: the committee view.

quote: I think—and many of my colleagues think—it’s hard to look at the incoming data and say that policy’s significantly restrictive at this time.  It may be—it may be sort of loosely neutral, or it may be somewhat restrictive.
rationale: Doubts that policy is significantly restrictive, weakening the case for further cuts.

quote: We do think tariffs are likely to move through and be a one-time price increase.
rationale: Treats tariff inflation as a one-time price increase.

quote: Clearly, a weakening labor market calls for cutting; a stronger labor market says that the rates are in a good place.
rationale: Two-way conditional: weaker jobs mean cuts, stronger jobs mean rates are in a good place.

quote: Voted for the top of the fed funds target range at 3.75%; decision 3.75% (hold 11-1).
rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against dovish dissent

quote: Today, the FOMC decided to leave our policy rate unchanged.  We see the current stance of monetary policy as appropriate to promote progress toward our maximum-employment and 2 percent inflation goals.
rationale: The Chair restates the decision and that the stance is appropriate.

quote: So I would say the rate is—you can characterize it as in the high end of neutral, or you can characterize it as perhaps mildly restrictive, even modestly restrictive.  No one knows for sure.  But it’s in that range where it’s somewhere around the borderline between restrictive and not.
rationale: Rate at the high end of neutral or mildly restrictive; no lean either way.

quote: In addition, it probably raises the neutral rate in, in the near term. You’re looking at—you’re not looking at something that would immediately call for lower rates or that would be lowering inflation.
rationale: AI investment raises the near-term neutral rate and does not call for lower rates.

quote: And tariffs should be, in theory, unless they cause people to start expecting still more tariffs the next year and still more tariffs the next year, they should be a classic one- time thing.
rationale: Tariffs should be a one-time price effect.

quote: Inflation has moved up and is elevated, in part reflecting the recent increase in global energy prices.
rationale: Inflation has moved up with energy prices.

quote: The labor market shows more and more signs of stability, whereas inflation is kind of misbehaving.  And so maybe a little bit of restriction or the high end of neutral is just the right place to be.  So we can wait here and see—and see how things work out before we act.
rationale: Inflation misbehaving and jobs stable: content to hold and wait rather than ease.

quote: We’re a little north of 3½ [percent], so that’s well in the range of what I would consider reasonable, but at the higher end of the range of what I would consider reasonable neutral rate.  You know, I think you’re—the labor market is still probably cooling off just a little bit.  And I don’t think there’s much of a case for—any case, really—for, for policy looking, you know, meaningfully restrictive.
rationale: Sees no case for meaningfully restrictive policy, arguing against tightening.

rationale: majority vote for a hold at 3.75% at a split meeting, against hawkish dissent

rationale: dissent for a cut of 25bp to 3.5% against a majority hold at 3.75%
